title: Opportunistic decode shim for kernel-aware model routing and retry policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a low-latency speculative decode path that can opportunistically use faster model variants / kernels for the initial prefill + early decode tokens, but fall back deterministically if the tentative output is likely to diverge or violate quality SLOs. Current router designs either (a) always prefer the faster variant and incur user-visible regressions under certain prompts or (b) run parallel decodes which double cost.

Goal: Implement an 'opportunistic decode shim' that: (1) selects an initial kernel/model variant by kernel fingerprint and recent acceptance statistics, (2) emits a compact acceptance signal during early decode (first N tokens) that is cheaply computable, (3) defines a soft-accept / soft-reject decision window with hysteresis and backoff, and (4) provides a rollback/fast-retry fallback that completes remaining tokens on a conservative variant while preserving latency SLOs and minimizing duplicated compute.

Design summary:
- Kernel-aware initial selection: map model+input fingerprint to an affinity score derived from per-kernel latency histograms, recent acceptance rate, and quantized memory pressure indicators. Use a small MRU cache at the request router to avoid repeated scoring for identical prompt fingerprints.
- Early acceptance metric (A_delta): a lightweight signal computed from prefix log-prob deltas and confidence envelope across top-k tokens for the first 6 tokens. A_delta is normalized per-model and converted to a 0..1 score using running z-score windows.
- Soft thresholds: soft-accept if A_delta >= 0.72 and soft-reject if A_delta <= 0.42. Between these thresholds the decision remains 'probation' until token 12. Probation decay uses exponential smoothing with lambda=0.35.
- Fallback semantics: on soft-reject, switch to conservative variant for remaining tokens and mark request as 'partially rolled back' in trace metadata. If conservative variant produces identical output for last M tokens (M=4), we stamp 'rollback reconciled' otherwise mark 'diverged' and increment incident counter. In the reconciled path we avoid re-sending client events; in diverged path we provide an explanatory response header and create a follow-up telemetry sample for prompt-augmentation diagnostics.
- Cost control: opportunistic path has an adaptive budget per customer (tokens/month) and aborts opportunistic attempts if budget exceeded; fallbacks cost accounted to same request to avoid double-billing surprises.

Metrics / Acceptance:
- Primary acceptance metric: ProbAcceptanceRate = fraction of requests where opportunistic variant completed without rollback. Target >= 92% on sampled production traffic for tier-1 workloads.
- Latency improvement: median tail (P95) step-down of 8-12% for opportunistic routes vs conservative baseline.
- Quality safety: human-eval regression rate <= 0.5% on held prompt set; automated BLEU/ROUGE-like similarity delta thresholds for deterministic workloads.
- Observability: trace flag 'opport_decision' has fields [initial_variant, A_delta, decision, fallback_reason]. Chart in Grafana: grafana.redwood.ai/d/opport/overview

Rollout plan:
1) Canary internal traffic (Dev + Staging) — run for 2 weeks, collect A_delta distributions and reconciliation rates.
2) Small customer pilot (5 customers) with opt-in via Console toggles. Monitor ProbAcceptanceRate and customer SLOs for 4 weeks.
3) Scale to broader sample using adaptive budget caps and per-customer thresholds.
4) Full platform rollout contingent on meeting acceptance & human-eval thresholds and completing security review.

Testing & validation: unit tests for A_delta computation, simulation harness to replay historical requests through the shim with golden conservative variant outputs, cost accounting integration tests, and end-to-end performance benchmarks on target hardware (A100-80GB and T4).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: A_delta poorly calibrated across new models leading to high divergence. Mitigation: add per-model calibration phase with offline replay and automatic threshold tuning.
- Risk: double compute spikes during high traffic. Mitigation: global token budget + local request queueing + backpressure to client with 429 when opportunistic budget exhausted.

Open decisions:
- Finalize token window sizes N (prefill window) and M (reconciliation lookback). Proposal: N=12, M=4 (requires empirical validation).
- Whether to persist acceptance state for prompt templates across requests to improve stability.

2026-02-25: Design review with Security & Product. Security requested a KMS audit for any preserved prompt fingerprints (handled by MRU TTL + hashing). Action: add privacy note to spec.

2026-03-09: Canary started on staging cluster (A100 pool). Observed ProbAcceptanceRate=89% initially for long-form prompts; investigating prefill token distribution effect.
2026-03-12: Tuned smoothing lambda from 0.2 -> 0.35; ProbAcceptanceRate increased to 91.3% in staging. Preparing pilot customer checklist.
2026-03-13: Engineering review with Diego, Maya, and Priya: approved rollout gating criteria but postponed automatic per-model threshold tuning until post-pilot.
